title: New insights into single-grain mechanical behavior from temperature-dependent 3-D coherent X-ray diffraction

nodes.label: How strain heterogeneities build up inside one embedded grain under thermomechanical load has never been mapped in 3-D
3-D coherent X-ray diffraction with phase retrieval on a single grain during thermal cycling should resolve the intra-grain displacement field and its reversibility
Au polycrystalline film, 475 nm, on fused silica: strong scatterer, elastically very anisotropic, oxidation-free

attrs.reason: scattering power, anisotropy A=2.9, no oxidation

nodes.label: 3-D CXD on one non-overlapped grain peak of a FIB-isolated 15x15 um island, 2x2 um focused beam, rocking around ex

attrs.note: headline method: it makes the intra-grain field measurable

nodes.label: Thermal cycling room temperature to 270 C in 25 C steps (about 0.03% strain per step), heating and cooling branches, two cycles

attrs.levels: 35-270 C in 25 C steps; 2 synchrotron cycles + 1 lab cycle

nodes.label: Physical vapour deposition of a 475 nm Au film on fused silica
Flame annealing at 800-900 C for 30 s to grow the grains laterally
Thermal cycling to 270 C loads the grain in compression on heating and tension on cooling through the Au/silica expansion mismatch
Grains are columnar: one grain spans the whole film thickness, boundaries running from the substrate to the surface
In-plane grain size 0.3-3 um; about 450 grains in the isolated island
{111} fibre texture with 5.03 deg FWHM spread about the surface normal; a few <100> grains
Neighbourhood of grain g1: g2, g4, g5 share its in-plane orientation and lie along y; g3 and g6 are in-plane misoriented and lie along x
Thermal loading stores defects (dislocations) in the grain, preferentially along x where the misoriented boundaries block transmission
The grain's out-of-plane lattice strain runs a hysteresis loop from -0.05% to about -0.17% over one cycle, far shallower than the thermo-elastic slope
Intra-grain strain heterogeneity is strongly anisotropic and grows with temperature: it develops along x in the film plane, stays weak through the thickness
The heterogeneity evolution is quasi-reversible on cooling, i.e. anelastic rather than a permanent plastic change
Misoriented neighbours g3 and g6, lying along x, accommodate stress at their grooved boundaries and trap defects there, building the x-direction heterogeneity
The method follows one buried grain through a full thermal cycle and returns both its average strain and its 3-D displacement field

attrs.condition: in-situ thermal cycling, 1 h per temperature step

nodes.label: A single grain carries large, anisotropic and quasi-reversible intra-granular strain heterogeneities set by its immediate neighbourhood, invisible to averaged diffraction
Apart from the first heating, the single grain follows the macroscopic film response measured with a laboratory source

attrs.verdict: single grain representative of the film after the first heating

nodes.label: Only the out-of-plane strain component is accessible in this geometry; shear components come only from displacement gradients, and one grain is measured
Cross-section: one grain spans the whole film thickness everywhere in the field, but the boundaries are curved, not straight walls

attrs.image_note: the grains are rounded in section and their boundaries curve; what the panel establishes is that a single grain spans the thickness, not that the boundaries stand normal to the substrate. the in-panel marker reads 0.372 um for the imaged thickness while the text states a 475 nm film; the section is a sample prepared under similar, not identical, conditions

panel_conditions.condition: cross-sectional SEM of a sample prepared under similar conditions

The {111} pole figure resolves individual grain maxima; one isolated, non-overlapped maximum (circled) is available for the CXD measurement

nodes.label: Out-of-plane strain rises with temperature and returns on a lower branch: the grain starts at -0.05% near 35 C and comes back to about -0.17% at 50 C

attrs.image_note: read from the green (synchrotron cycle 1) curve; the blue second cycle closes at about -0.18% at 50 C

nodes.label: None of the measured branches follows the ideal thermo-elastic line, which is about three times steeper than every measured cycle
The laboratory film cycle and the two single-grain cycles run within about 0.05% of each other above 150 C; during the first heating the grain stays near -0.05% while the film climbs steeply

panel_conditions.condition: red = laboratory source, many (111) grains; green = single-grain cycle 1; blue = single-grain cycle 2

nodes.label: The qx peak width grows monotonically from 1.35e-3 to 4.9e-3 A^-1 between 35 and 265 C
On cooling the qx width stays above the heating branch at every temperature and returns only to 1.95e-3 A^-1, 45% above the 1.35e-3 starting value

attrs.image_note: the two branches only merge above about 230 C; the residual offset at 50 C is the part of the broadening that does not recover

nodes.label: The size-only broadening of the grain is 6.61e-4 A^-1, two to seven times smaller than the measured qx widths

attrs.image_note: value read from the annotation printed inside panel (b); the comparison uses the measured dqx values of the same panel

attrs.image_note: the 50 C cooling map (e) recovers the y-striped character but is not identical to the initial 50 C map (a); the (xz) maps stay constant along z in every panel

Projected <110> in-plane directions: g1, g5, g4 and g2 fall within about 10 deg of each other, g6 lies some 15-20 deg and g3 some 25-30 deg away

attrs.image_note: angles measured off the drawn arrows of the panel; the paper tabulates the exact misorientations in Table 2, which is not in the packet

nodes.label: Converted to stress, the strains read from the figure give about 113 MPa at the start and about 380 MPa at the end of the cycle, against the 95 and 250 MPa quoted in the text

attrs.image_note: the quoted 250 MPa corresponds to eps = -0.11%, but the cycles close at -0.167% (green) and -0.183% (blue) at 50 C in panel (a)

nodes.label: Gold scatters X-rays strongly (high Z), has an elastic anisotropy factor near 2.9 and does not oxidise
Gold and fused silica have different thermal expansion coefficients, so a temperature excursion imposes an in-plane strain on the film
Scherrer relation dq_size = 2 pi / L gives the broadening due to grain size alone
Phase retrieval on an oversampled diffraction pattern (Sayre; iterative algorithms) recovers the complex amplitude and hence the displacement field
For an equibiaxial stress state sigma = -eta_111 M_111 eps_perp, with M_111 = 188.6 GPa and eta_111 = 1.2

notes: Method paper: the headline is the measurement, so DES/method (a4) is on the spine and realizes the intra-grain heterogeneity claim (a16), and the PRF node (a19) is the capability of the method rather than of the material. Two branches meet at a16: the processing/structure branch (PVD -> anneal -> columnar grains, neighbourhood orientations) and the loading branch (thermal cycling -> average strain, defect storage). Lost: Tables 1 and 2 (peak widths per direction, exact misorientations) are not in the packet, so the direction-resolved width comparison is carried by F4b plus the text. Panel-section problems: the F2b and F7b crops are labelled 'letter q (OCR DISAGREES with detector b)' - both are really (b). Figure-level problems: F3 panel (f) is axis-labelled dqz vs dqy although the caption calls it a qz-perpendicular slice; the F1b cross-section carries a 0.372 um thickness marker against a stated 475 nm film; converting the F4a strains with the paper's own modulus relation gives 113 and 380 MPa where the text quotes 95 and 250 MPa (o18).

changes: o1: label and image_note corrected - the F1b cross-section shows rounded grains with curved boundaries spanning the film thickness, not boundaries running straight from substrate to surface
a10: label softened from 'boundaries normal to the substrate' to 'boundaries running from the substrate to the surface', which is what F1b shows

panel_checks.note: F1b is the cross-sectional SEM; the 0.372 um in-panel marker against the stated 475 nm film is real, as the node's image_note says. Only the 'straight boundaries' wording needed correction.

dqx rises from about 1.35e-3 at 35 C (red, heating) to 4.9e-3 at 265 C; the printed dq^Size = 6.61e-4 annotation that o12 reads is in the same panel, and the cooling branch returns to about 1.95e-3, as o11 states
the <110> projection diagram carries g1/g5, g4, g2 within about 10 deg of each other, with g6 and g3 further away on opposite sides, as the node states

review.audit_summary: 3 audits (a22 method limitation, o11 non-recovering peak width, o18 stress conversion that does not reproduce the text's 95/250 MPa). All three change the support of a spine claim and are stated as arithmetic or figure readings, not as accusations. The o18 conversion checks out: 1.2 x 188.6 GPa x 0.0005 = 113 MPa and x 0.00167 = 378 MPa.
